subject: [PATCH RFC v4 11/12] mm/gup: batch contiguous PTE-mapped large folios in follow_page_mask()

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David questioned the necessity of including this patch in the current patch set, suggesting it could be submitted independently.
reviews.raw_body:
Why is this patch part of this patch set?

This makes perfect sense independently, no?

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author agreed to drop the patch and re-introduce it in a future version as part of another optimization, citing code entanglement issues.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm happy to drop this for now. I think it would
fit in better with another optimization to only
take one refcount per continuously mapped extent
of pages from the same folio.

I can't really untangle it because it modifies
some of the same code as other patches in the
series, but I'm happy to save it for a follow-up.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of PTE-mapped large folios in the Linux kernel's memory management system by batching contiguous pages together, reducing the number of page table walks required. This is achieved through a new function called `folio_pte_batch_flags()` that counts consecutive present PTEs mapping consecutive pages with uniform write bits. The patch improves performance for large anonymous regions, specifically 64 kB mTHP mappings, which see a 7.6x reduction in get time.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David suggested applying the optimization from patches 10 and 11 upfront in this series, assuming it will benefit many use cases that pin multiple consecutive pages.
reviews.raw_body:
Given this series here is RFC, can't we have that optimization upfront? I'd
assume it will benefit quite some use cases that pin multiple consecutive pages.

IIUC, it'd be mostly patch 10+11. No need to worry about the test case right
now, we can do that later.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author agreed to send patches 10-11 separately, deferring a self test until a future optimization is implemented.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm happy to send patches 10-11 by themselves.

We can save a self test for after the future
optimization of only taking a single refcount
for an entire extent of pages from the same
folio mapped in the same process, at which
point we'll have something more serious to
test.

I'll get these to you soon.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.
